newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power prices steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power prices steady to lower.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. were steady to lower Monday versus Friday's levels amid easing natural gas prices and return of a couple of nuclear generating stations from refueling.
Short-term physical natgas prices weakened further today after Friday's losses on forecasts of weather in the eastern U.S. moderating from a recent cool spell.
In the key U.S. Gulf production region, swing natgas prices fell about five cents from Friday to the $2.70 per million British thermal unit mark.
The 1,137 megawatt (MW) Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y., was in process to resume full output from its autumn refueling outage that began September 28.
The 510 MW Vermont Yankee nuclear power station in Vernon, Vt., will likely resume full production later today after more than a week's delay from its original startup from refueling shutdown.

Effect of more cheap generating capacity was mitigated by still firm residual fuel oil prices in the Northeast and a planned outage of a 765 kilovolt (KV) transmission power line from Quebec to New York, marketers and traders said.

The New York Power Authority (NYPA) scheduled to shut two portions of the transmission line late last week. The segments of the entire line, which has a capacity to carry 2,350 MW of electricity, were expected to return to service Friday.

In the western part of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) district, peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday was assessed at $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), down from Friday's $24.00-$25.00 quote for Monday delivery.
Western NYPP power for non-firm delivery during light load hours on Tuesday was stayed steady in the $14.00-$15.00 range.
In the eastern part of NYPP, peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday delivery was again pegged at $29.00-$31.00.
Off-peak, non-firm Tuesday electricity in eastern NYPP was again pegged near $17.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Tuesday at the Northeast Utilities border was discussed at $32.00-$33.00, lower than Friday's range of $33.00-$35.00 for Monday.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Tuesday delivery to the NU border was quoted at $18.00-$21.00, down from Friday's $20.00-$21.00 range.
In eastern half of NEPOOL, non-firm, next-day power for heavy demand hours was offered at $38.00-$40.00, and for light demand hours near $30.00.

According to the latest forecasts, temperatures in the Northeast would be within or slightly above seasonal range through mid-week, but a blast of arctic air would cause the thermometer to plummet toward the end of the weather.
